author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: The current request can leave the Library permanently loading when option hydration fails.
findings.consequence: If a same-version option failure could return a null accepted state, the early return would leave loading true.
findings.evidence: Installed Nuxt 4.4.8 provides no runtime producer for that same-version null state: fetchLibraryOptions converts HTTP and network failures to successful fallback options; a propagated DOMException AbortError follows Nuxt AsyncData's abort path and leaves execute unresolved rather than continuing to this branch; app-owned clear occurs on unmount only after requestVersion is invalidated; repeated in-component execution uses dedupe defer and does not abort.
findings.recommendation: No production change. Retain the existing fallback and request-version ownership behavior, and reassess if the installed AsyncData lifecycle changes.
findings.resolution: Withdrawn after independent runtime-aware adjudication: supported failures settle through fallback, while abort paths either never resume here or are already stale.
verification: Inspected app/pages/bibliotek.vue requestStateAfterOptions, runBrowserRequest, fetchLibraryOptions, disposal, and requestVersion ownership at HEAD 17cac069.
Inspected installed Nuxt 4.4.8 AsyncData execute, dedupe, clear, and AbortError behavior.
Confirmed HTTP and network failures are normalized by fetchLibraryOptions into a successful fallback response.
Confirmed app-owned options clear occurs after disposeLibraryRequest increments requestVersion.
Independent read-only runtime adjudication at HEAD 17cac069; no repository source or test files were modified.
Prior real Chromium audit verified HTTP 503 and browser network failure settle loading and render fallback Library results.
Prior synthetic AbortError audit verified Nuxt AsyncData execute does not resume the cited post-await branch.
